# otto

Leipzig, Germany. 58. Masters rower, cyclist at the weekend, member of a club
whose equipment he shares with everyone else in it. The record runs from
2029-08-01 to 2030-06-30.

## What he is for

Evidence. Every other persona's numbers arrive by connector or by hand, and
the record either holds a value or it does not. Otto photographs the rowing
machine's console at the end of a piece, so a figure in his record can be
looked at again.

That distinction is load-bearing and nothing else in the corpus exercised it.
A photo-read and a connector-read of one console on one evening are two claims
with one origin and two different error modes: the photo passed through an act
of reading and can be misread, and the evidence survives and can be re-read.

## The club machine

The ergometer is not his. Several people use it, nobody calibrates it, and the
drag factor is wherever the last person left it. A distance off that console
is a proxy for whatever the setting was that evening, and his record says so
rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

## What he measures that is not weight

A cloth tape four times a year, standing, at the navel, breathing out - stated
as a protocol and named on every row. One DEXA scan in January. One scan is a
point and not a trend, and his record is the corpus's only place where that
distinction has any rows to stand on.

## What he does not have

No injury, no goal beyond showing up twice a week through the winter, no
narrative arc. He is a record about how numbers arrive, not about what happens
to a person.
